brief: GS's Garrett argues SPX has stopped acting as risk's clearing price. Cross-asset correlations to the index have broken down, with bonds, rates, oil and consumer sentiment all telling a different story while SPX implied vol stays low. He attributes this to SPX becoming a self-contained asset class driven by AI vs non-AI dispersion rather than macro transmission, producing credit and rates anxiety despite calm index moves. Barron's flagged the divided market as scary. The Stock Trader's Almanac sees no near-term P&L risk, but Garrett's trench conversations and positioning data suggest otherwise. The top 10 stocks are expected to drive over two-thirds of S&P earnings growth this season. The desk broadened hedges beyond SPX puts, using IWM, HYG, TLT and SPXxAI downside, and flags an extreme Russell 2000 short that could squeeze if yields fall, hedged via a dual-digital payout. Fundamental long-short net leverage is near a five-year low though gross exposure stays high, and hedge funds rotated into TMT stocks in September. NDX hit a new all-time high. The desk favors NDX and QQQ upside exposure and QQQ over IWM outperformance.
